source.publication: 2025 MI-1040 Forms and Instructions (includes Form 4884 instructions)
source.section: PDF page 19 'Which Benefits are Taxable' (older spouse's year of birth on a joint return); PDF page 22 Line 19 ('If the older of you (or your spouse ...) was born during the period from January 1, 1946 through December 31, 1966'); Worksheet 3.3 (PDF page 25); MI-1040 lines 9a, 10, 13-17 (PDF page 10 Line 9a, Line 10, Line 17; PDF page 11 example: line 14 income subject to tax less line 15 exemptions = line 16 taxable income)

worked: Federal AGI = spouse 1 private pension 40,000.00 + spouse 2 wages 50,000.00 = 90,000.00. Federal taxable income = 90,000.00 - federal standard deduction (31,500.00) = 58,500.00; given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored. Michigan: the pension belongs to the spouse born 1968 (alone, no subtraction: born after 1966), but the older spouse was born 1965, so Section D applies to the return: Worksheet 3.3 line 4 = 75% x 131,794.00 = 98,845.50 (98,846 on line 19); line 5 40,000.00; line 6 40,000.00 to Schedule 1 line 27. Line 14 = 90,000.00 - 40,000.00 = 50,000.00; exemptions 11,600.00; line 16 = 38,400.00. MI-1040 line 17 tax = 38,400.00 x 0.0425 = 1,632.00. No credits; state income tax 1,632.00. (Without the older-spouse rule: taxable 78,400.00, tax 3,332.00.)
